around.headline: Bengaluru techie dies, partner injured after 7th-floor fall during dispute
around.summary: A software engineer died and his partner was injured after both fell from the 7th floor of a Bengaluru building following an argument, per NDTV and The Times of India. If you or someone you know is in a relationship reaching a crisis point, Karnataka's women's helpline (181) and police control room (112) are free and confidential — use them before things escalate.

around.headline: Two-wheelers, autos banned on KIA and Electronic City elevated corridors from September 4
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police announced two-wheelers will be barred from the KIA and Electronic City elevated corridors, with goods vehicles and autos also restricted on several major flyovers, effective September 4, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. If you ride a two-wheeler or auto through these stretches, check the full flyover list now and work out an alternate route before the deadline.

around.headline: ₹558 crore lost to cyberfraud in Karnataka this year — only ₹1.9 crore recovered
around.summary: State police data shows Karnataka has lost ₹558 crore to cyberfraud in 2026 so far, with barely ₹1.9 crore recovered, per The Times of India. Recovery odds are highest only in the first "golden hour" after a fraud — report immediately via the 1930 helpline or cybercrime.gov.in rather than waiting.

around.headline: KPSC veterinary exam scam widens: political functionary detained in Delhi
around.summary: A day after IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar was arrested and grilled by CID till midnight over irregularities in a KPSC veterinary recruitment exam, a political party functionary was detained in Delhi in the same case, per The Times of India. A reminder that competitive-exam results can face years of legal scrutiny if malpractice later surfaces.

around.headline: 'Save Lalbagh' protests swell against Parks Amendment Bill's land-diversion clause
around.summary: Thousands marched through Lalbagh against a state bill that could allow land inside Bengaluru's parks to be diverted for other use, per Deccan Herald and The News Minute. If you value the city's green spaces, this bill is worth tracking as it moves through the legislature.

around.headline: 14 Kannadigas still untraced in flood-hit Nepal; two have returned safely
around.summary: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar said 14 Kannadigas remain untraced in Nepal after this week's flash floods, though two have safely returned, as the disaster's toll continues to climb, per The Times of India. If you have family or friends travelling in Nepal, check in on them and watch for state helpline updates.

street_smart.title: A WhatsApp message offers you a 'work-from-home job' — simple data entry or product reviews, ₹2,000–5,000 a day. The recruiter, with a company logo and HR-sounding name, says you just need to pay a small 'registration' or 'security deposit' to unlock your task dashboard — fully refundable after your first week. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds fits the choice-based trap format cleanly (today's real news — a 7th-floor fall during a dispute, the KPSC exam scam, Lalbagh land protests, new flyover restrictions, and Nepal flood updates — is either too tragic or too civic/administrative for a personal 'best move' scenario). Rotating in from the evergreen list: fake job offers & deposit fraud. This hasn't appeared as the street-smart topic in the last three weeks, which instead covered BESCOM impersonation (08-29 evening), bank-OTP calls (08-29 morning), digital-arrest video calls (08-28 morning), phone snatching (08-28 evening), a dating-app meetup robbery (08-30 morning), and unregulated 'peptide party' wellness injections (08-30 evening).
street_smart.situation: A group chat full of other 'employees' is posting screenshots of daily payouts, the recruiter replies within seconds to every question, and they push you to pay today because slots are 'filling up fast'.

choices.text: Don't pay anything upfront. Independently verify the company (official website, GST/CIN, MCA records, genuine reviews) — legitimate employers pay you, you never pay them to get hired.
choices.feedback: Correct. The moment money is expected to flow from you to an employer before you've earned anything, it's not a job — it's a funnel. Real employers cover their own costs and never charge candidates a 'registration', 'security', or 'unlock' fee at any stage.

choices.text: Pay the small registration fee — it's refundable anyway, and the group chat shows real people getting paid.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. The 'payouts' in the group chat are typically fake screenshots or a handful of early participants paid out deliberately to build trust and pull in more victims. Once you pay, the 'refundable' deposit is never returned, and you'll be asked for further fees — a 'tax', a 'penalty', an 'unlock charge' — at every stage until you stop paying or run out of money.

choices.text: Pay the fee, but first ask the recruiter for a written refund policy.
choices.feedback: A document from an anonymous WhatsApp recruiter is worth nothing — they'll ignore it or simply vanish once you've paid, and there's no real entity to hold to it. Written promises don't change who's on the other end of the chat.

choices.text: Complete the first task for free to test if it's real before paying anything.
choices.feedback: Better than paying blind, but scam operators often deliberately let you complete a few simple free tasks precisely to build trust before asking for the deposit. A free task doesn't verify the company — only the direction money flows does, and that direction should always be employer to you.

takeaways: Legitimate employers never ask you to pay to get hired, to 'unlock' tasks, or to receive your own earnings — money should only ever flow from employer to worker.
Verify any recruiter or company via MCA (mca.gov.in) or a GST/CIN lookup, and search the exact company name plus 'scam' before engaging further.

If you've already paid and suspect fraud, report immediately at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 — per today's report, Karnataka has recovered only about ₹1.9 crore of the ₹558 crore lost to cyberfraud this year, and reporting within the first 'golden hour' is what determines whether money is recoverable at all.

quiz.question: A political party functionary was detained in Delhi this week in connection with which Karnataka recruitment scam?
quiz.why: KPSC (Karnataka Public Service Commission) conducts the state's own civil service and department exams, separate from the UPSC exams for all-India services.

quiz.question: From September 4, Bengaluru traffic police are barring two-wheelers from which two elevated corridors, per today's report?
quiz.why: The restriction is part of a wider set of curbs that also limits goods vehicles and autos on several major city flyovers from the same date.

quiz.question: Karnataka's CM said today that how many Kannadigas remain untraced in flood-hit Nepal, though two have safely returned?
quiz.why: Nepal's flash floods, triggered by a glacial lake outburst, have caused widespread destruction and a rising death toll across the region this week.

quiz.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
quiz.why: Gujarat's coastline runs roughly 1,600 km, the longest of any Indian state, giving it major ports like Kandla and Mundra.

quiz.question: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance on Earth?
quiz.why: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon, but diamond's rigid crystal lattice makes it far harder — it ranks 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, the maximum possible.
